findings.title: Left-edge agreement depth depends only on v2(p) and is constant in t for v2(p)<=3: the constants are 8, 29, 400
findings.claim: In the moving integer frame from the single-cell seed, depth(t,p), the number of leading left-edge cells on which row t and row t-p agree, was identical for every tested p of the same 2-adic valuation and identical for every t in [3000,6000): 8 at v2=1, 29 at v2=2, 400 at v2=3. At v2(p)>=4 it is not constant in t. The 29-cell period-4 prefix independently corroborates the 26-cell common ether prefix assumed by the kernel-checked absorbing-prefix barrier, so that barrier hypothesis is generic on this orbit rather than a corner case.
findings.scope: Single black cell seed; Phi(a)=a XOR ((a<<1)|(a<<2)); rows high-bit aligned; T=6000; every t in [3000,6000); p in {2,6,10,14,4,12,20,28,36,44,8,24,40,56,72,16,48,80,32,96}. Pure enumeration.
findings.result: Ran. Constants reproduce exactly across all tested p within each valuation class and all t in range.

verification.limits: T=6000 rows; t restricted to [3000,6000); 20 periods; single seed; Python ints, no solver, no timeout reached; runtime under 5 minutes on one core.

limitations: Finite horizon. Constant to t<6000 is not a theorem for all t; assuming otherwise is exactly the error my round-1 response made.
Single seed and a single observation alignment (left edge, high-bit aligned). Not tested for other offsets.
No proof that v2 is the controlling parameter; it is an exact fit on 20 periods, not a derivation.
findings.next_action: Extend T by an order of magnitude to see whether 8, 29 and 400 survive, then attempt the v2 dependence as a lemma about the left-edge tiling.

findings.title: Sharp transition at v2(p)=4: the regular region goes from a bounded strip to a constant fraction (about 0.375) of the light cone
findings.claim: For v2(p)<=3 the agreement depth is a constant and its share of the cone (2t+1) tends to zero. For v2(p)>=4 the depth grows linearly in t, holding a fraction near 0.375 across t=1000 to t=7999, an eightfold range. At p=16 the fraction read 0.385, 0.377, 0.381, 0.378, 0.376. Therefore roughly three eighths of every row lies in a period-16 regular region that begins beyond the 29-cell strip, entirely outside what a prefix reader absorbing on the ether prefix can observe.
findings.result: Ran. Fraction stable near 0.375 for v2>=4; p=8 control pinned at exactly 400 at t=1000, 4000 and 7999.

verification.limits: T=8000 rows; five t values; six periods; no solver; runtime under 5 minutes on one core.

limitations: Checked that this is not a cone artifact only by noting the fraction stays near 0.377 rather than approaching 1, and that the p=8 control stays flat. That is evidence, not proof.
Five sampled t values per period, not every t.
The fraction drifts slightly downward with p (0.376 at p=16 to 0.371 at p=128); I do not know whether that is real or a horizon effect.
I searched for a renormalization law relating 8, 29 and 400 and FAILED to find one. Ratios 3.6 and 13.8 fit nothing clean. Reported rather than curve-fitted.
findings.next_action: Establish whether the 0.375 fraction has an exact closed form, and whether the period-16 regular region admits a tiling description that can be stated in Lean.

findings.title: Proposed well-founded resource: Dershowitz-Manna multiset over non-regular blocks, with the period-16 regular region as the identity element
findings.claim: Proposal, not run. Take the F002 period-16 regular region as the identity, decompose the complement into maximal non-regular blocks, and order the finite multiset of blocks by Dershowitz-Manna under a per-block ordinal. This is not of the barred form: a DM multiset order is not a signed integer prefix energy with geometric per-letter costs, and the regular region is an identity element rather than an absorbing reader state. Ether insertion and long vacuum segments are rank-invariant by construction, and block mergers are safe because DM permits removing an element. MISSING LEMMA, stated exactly: for every Rule 30 step in which one non-regular block splits into two or more, each child is strictly below the parent in the chosen per-block ordinal. Splits are the only direction DM does not give for free.
findings.scope: Mechanism shape only. No per-block ordinal is defined, so no proof obligation is discharged.
limitations: No ordinal defined. Without one this is a shape, not a rank, and nothing is proved.
Rests on F002, which is a finite measurement.
The split lemma may simply be false; it has not been tested even empirically.
findings.next_action: Extract non-regular blocks against the period-16 tiling, log every split event, and test candidate ordinals for non-decrease on splits. If a child can equal or exceed its parent, F003 dies cheaply.
